about: The Studio's explanations, each a storyboard that the player (app/studio/player.js) plays scene by scene on its own page (studio/<id>/). Add one by adding its file here and an entry to this list (id, file, title, summary, line: one line for its card, cast: the characters on its card), then run node app/studio/twin.mjs; the schema is in README.md beside this file.

animations.title: What compression is
animations.summary: What travels to the model each time you say something to a chat assistant, what a cache changes, why a full conversation gets compressed, what is lost when it is, and how this team works so that the loss does not matter.
animations.line: What a chat assistant sends to its model each time you speak, why a long conversation gets compressed, what is lost, and why this team does not mind.

animations.title: How a fact gets onto this site
animations.summary: From a body deciding something to a row you can cite: a source publishes, a collector reads it and notes when, a curator labels it, it becomes a row with a permanent id, the build serves it. With two real cases from Storm Charles's timeline.
animations.line: From a body deciding something to a row you can cite, with two real cases from Storm Charles's timeline.

animations.title: One warning, opened three times
animations.summary: What "fractal" means for a graph, shown on one real node: IPMA's red rain warning for Lisbon as a node in this site's graph, as a record in IPMA's open data, and as IPMA's own alert message. Three worlds, three vocabularies, one warning.
animations.line: What "fractal" means for a graph, on one real node: a warning as our graph sees it, as IPMA's open data gives it, and as IPMA's own alert message.

animations.title: Two faces
animations.summary: Why this site has two fronts: the Weather face, clean and for anyone, and the data room, where everything read from outside is kept with its source. The one rule between them: the face draws only what the data room holds.
animations.line: Why the site has a clean Weather front and a data room behind it, and the one rule between them.

animations.title: Follow a word to its source
animations.summary: You read "Web Summit" on this site. Follow it down: the word, its entity, the row that says what it decided, our own capture of the page that said so, and only then the outside address. One real chain, walked link by link.
animations.line: From the words "Web Summit" down to our own capture of the page that said so, link by link, and where the chain is still short.

animations.title: The hand-over
animations.summary: One sentence from Dinis about memory, the librarian's pack, what the accountant measured, and five agents handing their work to fresh sessions of themselves: the long session beside the file system as memory, with this team's own numbers.
animations.line: A sentence from Dinis, the librarian's pack, what the accountant measured, and five agents handing over to fresh sessions: this team's own numbers.
